title: Elasticity Mindmap
notes: Hooke's law (F = kx) states that deformation is proportional to applied force within the elastic limit. The spring constant k (N/m) measures stiffness.…
**Hooke's law statement:** For small deformations, the extension (or compression) of an elastic body is directly proportional to the applied force: F = kx,…
**Force (spring) constant k:** k = F/x, measured in N/m. It measures the stiffness of the spring — a stiffer spring has a larger k and needs a bigger force…

subtopics.name: Key points
points: F = kx holds only within the elastic limit — marked by the straight-line region of the F–x graph.
k measures stiffness in N/m; a larger k is a stiffer spring.
Series springs combine like 1/k = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂ (softer).
Parallel springs combine like k = k₁ + k₂ (stiffer).
Energy stored in a stretched spring is ½kx² — the triangle under the F–x graph.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Hooke's law: F = kx
Spring constant: k = F/x (units N/m)
Series springs: 1/k = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂
Parallel springs: k = k₁ + k₂
Elastic potential energy: U = ½kx²; oscillation ω = √(k/m)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Hooke's law: F = kx within the elastic limit.
The spring constant k measures the force per unit deformation (N/m).
Series springs: 1/k_eq = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂ (combination is softer).

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: The force required to extend a spring doubles when the extension doubles (F = kx).
Combinations of springs are a guaranteed numerical question.
Finding k from a graph slope is a frequent NEB short question.
Spring constant from graph: k = slope of F–x line in the linear region.
Series/parallel: use the same rule as capacitors (series) and resistors (parallel).

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Hooke's law F = kx is valid only in the linear region of the F–x graph, up to the proportionality limit.

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Stress is force per unit area; strain is fractional deformation (dimensionless).
Elasticity = recovery of shape when the force is removed; plasticity = permanent deformation.
Stress is proportional to strain only within the elastic limit (Hooke's law, σ = Eε).
The stress–strain curve has six regions: proportional, elastic, yield, plastic, ultimate, fracture.
Ductile materials deform plastically before breaking; brittle ones break suddenly near the elastic limit.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Stress: σ = F/A (N/m² or Pa)
Strain: ε = Δl/l (dimensionless; ε_V = ΔV/V, shear ε = θ)
Hooke's law in stress–strain form: σ = Eε
Young's modulus: E = (F/A)/(Δl/l) = Fl/(AΔl)
Bulk modulus: B = −P/(ΔV/V); Shear modulus: G = τ/θ

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Stress is the internal force per unit area resisting deformation: σ = F/A.
Strain is the fractional change in dimension and is dimensionless: ε = Δl/l.
Within the elastic limit stress is proportional to strain (Hooke's law): σ = Eε.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Stress and strain numericals are a guaranteed exam topic — practice unit conversions (mm² → m²).
Labeling the stress–strain curve and identifying regions carries direct marks.
Young's modulus problems (extension of a wire) appear almost every year.
Remember: strain has NO units — a quick sanity check for MCQs.
To find E: rearrange to E = Fl/(AΔl) — compute σ then divide by ε.

subtopics.name: Key points
points: E, B, G all have units N/m² (Pa) — they differ by the type of deformation they describe.
E (stretching), B (volume), G (shape) measure the corresponding resistance of a material.
The three moduli are linked: E = 2G(1+σ) and E = 3B(1−2σ).
Liquids and gases have G = 0 (they cannot resist shear) — only solids have a shear modulus.
Compressibility is the reciprocal of B.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Bulk modulus: B = −P/(ΔV/V)
Shear modulus: G = (F/A)/θ = τ/θ
Relation: E = 2G(1 + σ) = 3B(1 − 2σ)
Combined: E = 9BG/(3B + G); compressibility k = 1/B

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Young's modulus E = Fl/(AΔl) measures resistance to longitudinal deformation.
Bulk modulus B = −P/(ΔV/V) measures resistance to uniform compression.
Shear modulus G = τ/θ measures resistance to change of shape.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: E, B, G definitions and units are certainty for short-answer questions.
Young's modulus wire problems remain the most-tested numerical.
The relation E = 2G(1+σ) is frequently used to find Poisson's ratio.
unit memory: all three moduli are in N/m² (Pa).
For Young's modulus: rearrange E = Fl/(AΔl) to solve any one variable.

❌ 'Shear strain is a length ratio.' ✅ Shear strain is the ANGLE of displacement θ (radians), not a length…
